items.followUp: Draw the truth table for “P OR Q.”

rubric.why: Shows all four possible input combinations.
rubric.description: Lists all possible combinations of P and Q.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark if the four input combinations are shown.

rubric.why: The AND operation is true only when both inputs are true.
rubric.description: Gives the correct output for each input combination.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark if all four outputs are correct.
Award 1 mark for identifying the act as intentional or deliberate.

rubric.why: The purpose is to harm or interfere with a computer system or its operation.
rubric.description: Identifies damage to or disruption of a computer system or its operation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the harm or disruption caused.

modelAnswer: Sabotage is the deliberate act of damaging a computer system, its data or network, or disrupting its normal operation.

rubric.why: Cipher text is produced by applying encryption to a message.
rubric.description: States that cipher text is an encrypted or enciphered message.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as encrypted text.

rubric.why: Encryption makes the original message difficult to understand unless it is decrypted.
rubric.description: Explains that it cannot normally be understood without decryption or the key.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that the original message requires decryption or a key to read.

modelAnswer: Cipher text is the encrypted form of an original message (plain text).
It is not normally understandable until it is decrypted using the appropriate key.

rubric.why: A network of networks consists of networks linked together.
rubric.description: States that multiple networks are interconnected.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing networks as connected or interconnected.

rubric.why: The Internet is the common example of a network of networks.
rubric.description: Identifies the Internet as a network of networks.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the Internet.

modelAnswer: A network of networks is a system formed by interconnecting many computer networks.
The Internet is the largest example of a network of networks.

items.followUp: What is the function of POP3?

rubric.why: SMTP is the abbreviation for Simple Mail Transfer Protocol.
rubric.description: Gives the full form of SMTP.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct full form.

rubric.why: SMTP is used to send email.
rubric.description: States that SMTP is used for sending electronic mail.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying its email-sending function.

modelAnswer: SMTP stands for Simple Mail Transfer Protocol.
It is the protocol used to send email over the Internet.

items.followUp: What is an IP address used for when data travels across the Internet?

rubric.why: Internet data is divided into packets that are forwarded through the network.
rubric.description: States that data is sent in packets.

rubric.why: Routers use destination addressing to forward packets along a route.
rubric.description: Explains that routers forward packets using their destination address.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning routers and destination-based forwarding.

modelAnswer: Data is divided into packets, each carrying the destination IP address.
Routers read this address and forward each packet along a suitable route toward its destination.

rubric.why: This is the text before the HTML line-break tag.
rubric.description: Gives the first part of the paragraph correctly.

rubric.why: This is the text after the line-break tag.
rubric.description: Gives the second part on a new line.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for showing “a paragraph” after a line break.

items.followUp: Are HTML tag names case-sensitive? Give an example.

rubric.why: HTML treats uppercase and lowercase tag names alike.
rubric.description: States that HTML is not case-sensitive.

rubric.why: An example demonstrates that differently cased forms are treated equivalently.
rubric.description:
Gives an example such as

and

being treated the same.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct example or equivalent explanation.

modelAnswer: HTML is not case-sensitive, so uppercase and lowercase letters in tag names are treated alike.

For example,

and

represent the same paragraph tag. Lowercase tags are generally preferred.
